zumper.title: Served a purpose but ...

I used this app frequently in my 3 month search for an apartment and it was fine. My problem is with the number of emails I would receive daily - sometimes 10+ emails, not including the confirmation emails that follow immediately after sending an inquiry or reply to a posting. By default, every time you contact someone you are added to a list and will receive emails every day with other listings. You have to opt out of receiving them every single time.  

Despite that annoyance - which I largely blame myself for because I didn't notice that I could deselect the annoying emails after sending an inquiry - I found the app useful. But ... now I can't get them to stop sending 10+ emails every day even though I have changed my communication preferences to no further contact. 

Worse - I have started to receive emails based on my internet or Facebook history and not based on searches done with the Zumper app. It is still tracking my usage, so I am going to have to uninstall the app completely. I didn't want to do that because I only signed a short term lease so I will need to start searching for another place in a few months.  

Bottom line - the app does what you want it to do, but it also does what you don't want it to do. You have to decide which one of those things is more important to you.

kijiji.title: Not the same anymore...
kijiji.text:
Kijiji used to be a wonderfully effective way to buy & sell goods in Canada, but the company has implemented a couple new policies that have made it increasingly difficult for buyers and sellers to operate effectively:

The Review System - An absolutely horrible addition to Kijiji, this system allows scalpers and lowballers to waste your time sending absurdly low offers, then turning around and leaving negative reviews for not accepting their ridiculous offers. Kijiji customer service tells you to ignore people who do this, but sometimes you cannot ascertain this motive within 7 messages (the amount of messages before a review can be left), and end up suffering to a bad reputation as a result. If you leave your cell phone number as an alternative so you don’t fall into this trap... they’ll put your number into a robo-call system to harass you instead. Well done Kijiji!

Commercial Posting - Kijiji has become flooded with retailers posting their ads several times, even in the same region, which ends up flooding the pages with the same overpriced ads that shove all of the private (actual people) sellers to the bottom of the category ranks where they lose all visibility to prospective buyers. Incredibly anti-consumer move that I cannot understand.

These are the two major points that make Kijiji a nightmare to navigate, buy, and sell, and while I have been assured by customer service that this is being looked into, I won’t hold my breath.

realtorca.title: Now it’s an advertising platform
realtorca.text:
Every listing has an ad for TD insurance now. “See how much you can save with TD!” Over time no doubt there will be others. There will be more. 

This ad platform was a forced upgrade: it blocked all UI input until you upgraded. Just in case there was any doubt about the people behind this app and their motives. Why provide a service making money legitimately when you could leverage users’ attention to sell them to advertisers? Realtor.ca gets ad revenue. Advertisers get another platform to shove their commercial messaging in front of peoples’ eyeballs.  That’s the definition of win-win, right? Right???

Imagine a world where apps like this— already commercial speech in the form of advertising for houses— didn’t try to squeeze every penny out of every possible transaction, every user, everywhere all of the time. Imagine the people running it just said “this app is already advertising for our core business, no need to turn a catalog into a catalog with banner ads, what’s next, ads within ads within ads? Don’t we need to draw a line”?

If we make it to the end of the year without them adding auto playing video ads I will be shocked.

But think how much you can save!
